# `arecord -D hw:0,1` → EIO: where the "WCD Capture" path actually breaks

Board: Redmi K30 5G (`picasso`, SM7250), mainline 7.3.0-rc7 (`e1927d6cbd57-dirty`, #203) +
Denial Mobile, RAM-booted. Card: `0 [XiaomiRedmiK305]: sm8250 - Xiaomi-Redmi-K30-5G`,
`00-00 MultiMedia1 playback`, `00-01 MultiMedia2 capture`, mixer state applied as described in the
task (`MultiMedia2 Mixer TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3=1`, `TX DEC0 MUX=SWR_MIC`, `TX SMIC MUX0=ADC0`,
`TX_AIF1_CAP Mixer DEC0=1`, `TX_DEC0 Volume=84`).

## 0. TL;DR

* The `EIO` is **not** returned by `q6afe`, `q6asm` or the ADM. It is generated by the ALSA core:
  `wait_for_avail()` in `sound/core/pcm_lib.c` waits
  `max(100, buffer_size*1100/rate)` = **176 ms** for the first period, never gets a wake-up, and
  returns `-EIO` (`sound/core/pcm_lib.c:1952`, `:2027`). `arecord` only prints that errno.
* With an explicit `snd_pcm_start()`, the whole kernel-side chain reports success
  (AFE port `0xB037` started, ASM stream running, ADM matrix map acknowledged, swr2 clocked and
  active, TX macro MCLK/FS/SWR bits on) — and the **DSP still delivers exactly the
  `runtime->periods` (8) buffers that `q6asm_dai_prepare()` queued, all zero, and then never
  completes another `ASM_DATA_CMD_READ_V2`**. So the capture source is dead, not the ALSA plumbing.
* Root cause found in code: the WCD9385's SoundWire **source ports are only ever enabled by the
  codec's own mixer switches** (`"ADC1..4 Switch"`, `"DMIC0..7 Switch"`, `"MBHC Switch"`), because
  `wcd938x_sdw_hw_params()` builds the `sdw_stream_add_slave()` port list **only** from
  `wcd->port_config[]`, and the only writer of that array is `wcd938x_set_swr_port()`
  (`sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x.c:1863` → `:417` → `:398`). The applied route contains **only TX-macro
  controls**, no codec switches ⇒ `wcd->active_ports == 0` ⇒
  `sdw_stream_add_slave(..., 0, ...)` (`sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x-sdw.c:84-120`) ⇒ the codec drives
  nothing on the TX SoundWire lanes ⇒ the TX macro's DIN FIFO never fills ⇒ the AFE codec-DMA TX
  port never produces a frame ⇒ the ASM capture stream stalls after the 8 pre-queued buffers ⇒
  userspace `read()` times out with `-EIO`.
* Fix is a **runtime control write, not a kernel rebuild** (§6.1); a one-hunk guard patch (§6.2)
  makes the failure impossible to misdiagnose again, and §6.3 closes the last silent failure path
  (`ASM_SESSION_CMD_RUN_V2` status is never checked).

## 1. Exact failing call chain

```
userspace  arecord 1.2.16 (alsa-utils)
  snd_pcm_readi()                                   (blocking, rw interleaved, 960 frames)
    ioctl SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_READI_FRAMES
      __snd_pcm_lib_xfer()                    sound/core/pcm_lib.c:2274
        state is PREPARED and size < runtime->start_threshold
          -> snd_pcm_start() is NOT called            :2330-2337
        avail = snd_pcm_avail() == 0
        wait_for_avail()                      sound/core/pcm_lib.c:1952
          wait_time = max(100, 7680*1100/48000) = 176 ms     :1962-1978
          schedule_timeout(176 ms) -> never woken ('runtime->tsleep' is only
          woken from snd_pcm_period_elapsed(), i.e. from a DSP READ_DONE event)
          tout == 0  ->  err = -EIO           sound/core/pcm_lib.c:2027
  <- -EIO   ->  "arecord: pcm_read:2285: read error: Input/output error"
```

`q6afe` cannot produce `-EIO` at all: `afe_apr_send_pkt()` maps *every* transport failure to
`-EINVAL` and a response timeout to `-ETIMEDOUT` (`sound/soc/qcom/qdsp6/q6afe.c:1073-1113`), and
`q6afe_dai_prepare()` maps failures to `-EINVAL` after printing
`"AFE enable for port 0x%x failed"` / `"fail to start AFE port"` (`q6afe.c:1716,1758`,
`q6afe-dai.c:443`). **None of those messages exists for any attempt.** The premise "q6afe_port_start
failed and someone turned it into EIO" is therefore false.

What *is* broken is one level down: no `ASM_DATA_EVENT_READ_DONE_V2`
(`sound/soc/qcom/qdsp6/q6asm.c:703` → `snd_pcm_period_elapsed()` in
`q6asm-dai.c:193-196`) is delivered after the first `runtime->periods` reads, so the ALSA waitqueue
is never woken and `wait_for_avail()` times out.

### 1.1 Start paths that *are* reached and return 0

| step | code | evidence it ran |
|---|---|---|
| FE prepare: map DMA, `q6asm_open_read()`, routing, enc-cfg, queue `periods` reads, state=RUNNING | `q6asm-dai.c:204-300` (`open_read` :262, `q6routing_stream_open` :276, `q6asm_enc_cfg_blk_pcm_format_support` :286, `q6asm_read` loop :293) | no `"q6asm_open_write failed"`/`"stream reg failed"`/`"CMD Format block failed"`; the 8 queued reads come back (§2) |
| BE prepare: `q6afe_cdc_dma_port_prepare()` + `q6afe_port_start()` for `TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3` = `0xB037` | `q6afe-dai.c:387-446` (`:430`, `:441`), `q6afe.c:1689`, `:1709` | see §1.2 — no error string, and prepare completed (DAPM stream event below ran) |
| ADM: copp open (`ADM_PATH_LIVE_REC`, 48000, 2 ch, 16 bit) + matrix map | `q6routing.c:389-452` (`:415-423`, `:445`), `q6adm.c:457` (`ADM_CMD_MATRIX_MAP_ROUTINGS_V5`) | `q6adm_matrix_map()` (waits for the reply) logs `"routing for stream %d failed"` at `q6adm.c:527,535` — absent. `q6adm_open()` (`q6adm.c:381`, called at `q6routing.c:422`) failure would have produced `"stream reg failed"` at `q6asm-dai.c:278` — absent |
| SoundWire stream prepare+enable | `sound/soc/qcom/sdw.c` `qcom_snd_sdw_prepare()` `sdw_prepare_stream()`/`sdw_enable_stream()` (`:157`) | `lpass-tx-mclk` enabled at 9.6 MHz, `3230000.soundwire` `runtime_status=active` (§2.4) |
| TX macro runtime PM + DAPM | `sound/soc/codecs/lpass-tx-macro.c` | registers `0x000=1` (MCLK_EN), `0x004=1` (FS_CNT_EN), `0x008=1` (SWR_CLK_EN) while capturing (§2.5) |
| ASM run | `q6asm-dai.c:346` → `q6asm.c:1002` `ASM_SESSION_CMD_RUN_V2` | *unverifiable by design*: `q6asm.c:629-631` maps this opcode to `ASM_CLIENT_EVENT_CMD_RUN_DONE` and **never looks at `result->status`** (status is checked only for the OPEN/SET_ENCDEC group, `:638-654`). See §6.3 |

### 1.2 Why "no error message" ⇒ AFE port start returned 0

`soc_pcm_prepare()` runs `snd_soc_link_prepare()` and then every `snd_soc_dai_prepare()` **before**
the DAPM stream event (`sound/soc/soc-pcm.c`, `__soc_pcm_prepare()`); any error aborts before the
codec/macro is powered. The TX macro *was* powered (§2.5: MCLK/FS/SWR enabled, q6afe vote clocks
prepared), therefore every DAI prepare — including `q6afe_dai_prepare()` →
`q6afe_port_start()` — returned 0. *(Inference, but a tight one.)*

## 2. Live evidence (read-only probing; commands and output excerpts)

All commands run as `ssh -i ~/.ssh/picasso_key root@<lan-ip>`. No file was written on the
phone; `arecord` reproduced the failure (allowed), plus `amixer` reads and libasound calls through
`python3 -` on stdin.

### 2.1 The reported failure, reproduced with no kernel-side error

```
# arecord -D hw:0,1 -f S16_LE -r 48000 -c 2 -d 1 /dev/null; echo RC=$?
Recording WAVE '/dev/null' : Signed 16 bit Little Endian, Rate 48000 Hz, Stereo
arecord: pcm_read:2285: read error: Input/output error
RC=1
# dmesg -T | tail -14
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] pcm_open: attach -> 0
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] soc_open: dai_startup TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3 -> 0
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] soc_open: dai_startup wcd938x-sdw-tx -> 0
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] soc_open: dai_startup SDW Pin0 -> 0
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] soc_open: dai_startup tx_macro_tx1 -> 0
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] q6asm-dai open: comp …apr:service@7:dais pdata ffff000086421c80 stream 1
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] soc_open: dai_startup MultiMedia2 -> 0
[Tue Nov 17 20:12:32 2026] pcm_open: constraints_complete -> 0
```
Nothing follows: no `AFE enable for port`, no `fail to start AFE port`, no `routing for stream`,
no `CMD Format block failed`.

`arecord` dies in **< 250 ms** (one 176 ms `wait_for_avail()` timeout); `/proc/asound/card0/pcm1c/sub0/status`
reads `closed` immediately afterwards, i.e. the stream is torn down before any period happens.

### 2.2 The stream is never started by a read of 960 frames (mirrors arecord)

`python3` + `ctypes` on libasound, `snd_pcm_set_params(S16_LE, RW_INTERLEAVED, 2 ch, 48000)`
sets `start_threshold = buffer_size`; a plain `readi(960)` then never auto-starts:

```
prepare 0 state 2            # 2 = PREPARED
read0 -5(Input/output error) state=2      # one 176 ms timeout each, 6 reads in 1.6 s
read1 -5(Input/output error) state=2
```

### 2.3 With an explicit start: 8 periods, all zero, then a permanent stall

```
start 0 state 3              # 3 = RUNNING
read0 960 … peak=0 first=(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
… read7 same …
# 150-period run:
read 7679 frames in 0.360s => 0.44x realtime, peak=0, nonzero_periods=0
err -5 at 8 state 3
```
7679 = `8*960 - 1`, i.e. `q6asm_dai_pointer()` (`q6asm-dai.c:482`) returned
`q6asm_get_hw_pointer()*period_size` = `8*960` and subtracted one (`q6asm-dai.c:482-489`). Exactly one buffer per
`q6asm_read()` queued in `q6asm_dai_prepare()` (`runtime->periods` = 8, see the `--dump-hw-params`
output below), and nothing after that:

```
RATE: [8000 48000]  PERIOD_SIZE: [480 1920]  PERIODS: [2 8]  BUFFER_SIZE: [960 15360]
HW Params of device "hw:0,1": … PERIOD_SIZE: 960  PERIODS: 8  BUFFER_SIZE: 7680
```

Pointer frozen for 3 s afterwards (8 periods of 20 ms would have elapsed 150 times):

```
t=0.25 avail_update=0 ['state: RUNNING', 'avail: 0', 'hw_ptr: 7679', 'appl_ptr: 7679']
t=1.26 avail_update=0 ['state: RUNNING', 'avail: 0', 'hw_ptr: 7679', 'appl_ptr: 7679']
t=3.03 avail_update=0 ['state: RUNNING', 'avail: 0', 'hw_ptr: 7679', 'appl_ptr: 7679']
```
`status->tstamp` stays `0.000000000` → not a single `snd_pcm_period_elapsed()` happened while the
stream was RUNNING. Control: before `snd_pcm_start()` the pointer is `hw_ptr 0` in `PREPARED` for
2 s, so the 8 completions come from the RUN path, not from `prepare`.

### 2.4 Everything on the LPASS side is up while the stream runs

`/sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary` sampled **during** the capture (stream `state: RUNNING`):

```
 LPASS_CLK_ID_TX_CORE_MCLK       4  4  0  19200000 …  txmacro@3220000
 LPASS_CLK_ID_TX_CORE_NPL_MCLK   4  4  0  19200000 …  txmacro@3220000
 LPASS_HW_MACRO / LPASS_HW_DCODEC 4 4  0         0  …  txmacro@3220000
    lpass-tx-mclk                1  1  0   9600000 …  3230000.soundwire   iface
# swr2 runtime: active
```

### 2.5 TX macro (regmap debugfs) idle vs capturing

```
            idle   capture
000: MCLK_EN     0        1
004: FS_CNT_EN   0        1
008: SWR_CLK_EN  0        1
090: FREQ_MCLK   1        1
0c0..0cc: SWR_DMICn_CTL  XXXXXXXX  0000000e
0d0/0d4: SWR_AMIC0/1_CTL XXXXXXXX  00000000
100/104: ADC_MUX0_CFG0/1  1        1
```
`0x0d0/0x0d4 == 0` is *not* a defect: the WCD9385 analog mics go through the **codec's** ADCs and
reach the TX macro over SoundWire (`"TX SWR_ADC0", "ADC1_OUTPUT"` in the board `audio-routing`);
the macro's own AMIC inputs are for mics wired to the LPI pads and are unused here.

### 2.6 The one hard anomaly on the bus: the TX slave is in Alert

```
/sys/bus/soundwire/devices/sdw:2:0:0217:010d:00:4/status -> Attached   (wcd_rx, swr1)
/sys/bus/soundwire/devices/sdw:3:0:0217:010d:00:3/status -> Alert      (wcd_tx, swr2)
```
Both SoundWire masters have identical defaults (`default_col=16`, `default_row=50`,
`max_clk_freq=9600000`), and the board's `swr1`/`swr2`/`txmacro`/`vamacro` nodes are field-for-field
identical to `upstream/linux/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sm8250.dtsi`, so this is not a DT frame-shape
error. `wcd_update_status()` (`sound/soc/codecs/wcd-common.c:102`) only resyncs the regcache on
`SDW_SLAVE_ATTACHED` and ignores `SDW_SLAVE_ALERT`, so once the flag is raised nothing ever clears it.

### 2.7 Vote/devote (the two `0x100f6` messages)

```
qcom-q6afe aprsvc:service:4:4: cmd = 0x100f6 returned error = 0x1
qcom-q6afe aprsvc:service:4:4: Unknown cmd 0x100f6        (x2 per close)
```
`0x100f6` = `AFE_CMD_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_DEVOTE_REQUEST` (`q6afe.c:52`). The ADSP answers it with
`APR_BASIC_RSP_RESULT`, which `q6afe_callback()` cannot match (`:1039-1041`), hence "Unknown cmd".
The VOTE (`0x100f4`, `q6afe.c:1949`, response `0x100f5`, `:1045`) is **accepted** — otherwise
`"AFE failed to vote"` (`:1961`) would appear and the tx-macro runtime resume would have failed.
Cause of the DE-vote rejection: `q6afe_vote_lpass_core_hw()` never reads the granted client handle
out of the VOTE response and never writes `*client_handle` (`q6afe.c:1928-1963`), so
`clk_vote_q6dsp_block()` stores an uninitialised handle (`q6dsp-lpass-clocks.c:85-105`,
`Q6DSP_VOTE_CLK` entries in `q6afe-clocks.c`), and `q6afe_unvote_lpass_core_hw()` sends
`client_handle = 0` (`q6afe.c:1914-1935`). Consequences: two error lines per stream close, and a
leaked vote — `LPASS_HW_MACRO`/`LPASS_HW_DCODEC` `prepare_cnt` stays at 4 across close.
**It happens at unprepare, after the capture already failed; it cannot be the cause of the EIO.**

### 2.8 The codec's SoundWire port list is built from the mixer, and only from the mixer

```
sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x.c:2588-2615   SOC_SINGLE_EXT("ADC1 Switch", WCD938X_ADC1, 1, 1, 0,
                                                     wcd938x_get_swr_port, wcd938x_set_swr_port)
                                       … same for ADC2..4, DMIC0..7, MBHC
sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x.c:1863        wcd938x_set_swr_port()  -> wcd938x_connect_port()
sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x.c:417         wcd938x_connect_port()  -> wcd938x_sdw_connect_port()
sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x.c:398         wcd938x_sdw_connect_port(): port_config->ch_mask |= ch_mask
sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x-sdw.c:84-120  wcd938x_sdw_hw_params(): copies only ports with ch_mask,
                                       then sdw_stream_add_slave(sdev, &sconfig, &port_config[0],
                                                                 wcd->active_ports, sruntime)
```
There is no other writer: `grep -rn channel_map sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x*` is empty, so
`qcom_snd_sdw_startup()` (`sound/soc/qcom/sdw.c:95-135`) gets `-ENOTSUPP` from
`snd_soc_dai_get_channel_map()` and consequently never calls `snd_soc_dai_set_channel_map()`.
With none of those switches on, `wcd->active_ports == 0` and the slave is attached to the stream
with **zero data ports**: it never drives its TX slots, the TX macro receives nothing, the AFE
`TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3` port never raises a DMA request, and the ASM capture stream stops after the
buffers that were queued in `prepare`.

## 3. Ranked hypotheses

| # | hypothesis | why it is ranked here |
|---|---|---|
| **H1** | **The WCD9385 TX SoundWire source ports were never enabled** (`ADC*/DMIC*/MBHC Switch` all off) ⇒ `active_ports == 0` ⇒ no TX data on the bus | Proven by code (§2.8) and it is the only explanation consistent with *every* other stage reporting success while the DSP stops exactly after the `prepare`-queued buffers. Fixable at runtime; one-mixer-write test in §7 |
| H2 | The AFE port started with a config the picasso ADSP accepts but does not honour (`q6dma_hw_params()` never fills `data_format`, `q6afe-dai.c:497-509`, and `q6afe_cdc_dma_port_prepare()` forwards it as 0, `q6afe.c:1689-1706`) | Same top-level symptoms; would survive H1's fix. Discriminate by re-testing after §7 step 2 |
| H3 | `ASM_SESSION_CMD_RUN_V2` was rejected and the failure was swallowed (`q6asm.c:629-631`) | Plausible design gap, but the 8 pre-queued reads *did* complete, which requires a running stream. Cheap to rule out with §6.3 |
| H4 | The `sdw:3` slave is wedged in `Alert` and its ports stay unusable even when enabled | Real, measured anomaly (§2.6); if H1's fix leaves the stall, the codec must be reset/re-enumerated and the alert serviced (`wcd_update_status()` ignores it) |
| H5 | Codec analog mic path not powered / gains at 0 / MIC BIAS off | Causes **zero-valued** data at the correct rate, i.e. a low RMS — *not* the missing periods. Must still be checked in §7 step 4 (as is `"TX0 MODE"`) |

Ruled out on the way (each has a loud error path that stayed silent): AFE port start failure,
ADM copp open failure, ADM matrix-map failure, DMA-buffer mapping failure, missing
`q6afe`/`txmacro` clocks, DT mismatch against upstream (the `wcd-capture-dai-link`, `swr2` port
arrays, `txmacro`/`vamacro` clock lists and 4-channel `SECONDARY_MI2S_RX` fixup special case in
`sound/soc/qcom/sm8250.c:57-82` all match `sm8250-mtp.dts`/`sm8250.dtsi`; `qcom,tdm-slot` is not
used on this link upstream either).

## 4. Answers to the five questions

1. **Where does the start fail?** Not in `q6afe_port_start()`/`q6afe_port_prepare()` and not in
   `q6asm_run()`; those succeed. The first observable failure is that the DSP stops delivering
   `ASM_DATA_EVENT_READ_DONE_V2` (`q6asm.c:703`) after the `runtime->periods` reads queued in
   `q6asm_dai_prepare()`. `-EIO` is then synthesised by `wait_for_avail()`
   (`sound/core/pcm_lib.c:2027`) 176 ms later. Cause: the codec's SoundWire TX ports are not
   configured (§2.8).
2. **Does the ADSP support the clock-vote protocol?** Yes for VOTE (`0x100f4`, accepted); DEVOTE
   (`0x100f6`) is rejected with `status=1` because mainline sends `client_handle = 0` — it never
   parses the handle from the VOTE response. There is no quirk or firmware-version check anywhere
   in `q6afe.c`/`q6afe-clocks.c`/`q6dsp-lpass-clocks.c`, and the failed devote is only logged
   (`q6afe_callback()` `:1039`); it does not leave the TX macro's `mclk`/`fsgen` unvoted *while
   streaming* (all enable counts are 1 during capture) — it leaks the MACRO/DCODEC block vote after
   close. Not the cause of the EIO.
3. **Does `sm8250_be_hw_params_fixup()` support the codec-DMA capture path?** Yes: for
   `cpu_dai->id != SECONDARY_MI2S_RX` it forces 48000 Hz / 2 ch / S16_LE
   (`sound/soc/qcom/sm8250.c:57-82`), which matches the FE (`--dump-hw-params`: 48000, 2 ch,
   S16_LE) and the ADM copp (`routing_hw_params()`, `q6routing.c:1129-1160`, gets
   `ADM_PATH_LIVE_REC`, 48000, 2, 16). Nothing invalid is left behind.
4. **Is the `WCD Capture` link missing something upstream has?** No. `cpu = <&q6afedai
   TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3>`, `codec = <&wcd9385 1>, <&swr2 0>, <&txmacro 0>`, `platform =
   <&q6routing>`, no `qcom,tdm-slot` — identical to `sm8250-mtp.dts:715-727`. What is missing is
   **runtime mixer state** (the codec switches), not DT.
5. **Is the VA-macro DMIC port (`VA_CODEC_DMA_TX_0`) a viable first capture path?** Yes, and it is
   the better bring-up path on this firmware: there is no SoundWire slave in the middle — the VA
   macro's DMIC front end is enabled by its own DAPM (plus `pinctrl-0 = <&tx_swr_active
   &dmic2_active &dmic3_active>` and `audio-routing "TX DMIC2", "MIC BIAS1"`), so it is immune to
   the H1 failure mode. It needs a DT change (a `VA Capture` back-end link with
   `cpu = <&q6afedai VA_CODEC_DMA_TX_0>` does not exist in the picasso DTS today), so it is a
   patch + rebuild, not a mixer write.

## 5. Why the 8 zero buffers arrive at all (mechanism, inferred)

`q6asm_dai_prepare()` queues `runtime->periods` `ASM_DATA_CMD_READ_V2` commands **before** the ASM
stream is started (`q6asm-dai.c:293`), each pointing at a freshly zeroed DMA buffer. When the
stream is RUN and the ADM copp has no data source, the DSP drains that queue once (the buffers come
back untouched = zeros) and then waits for its input; re-queued reads from
`event_handler()`/`ASM_CLIENT_EVENT_DATA_READ_DONE` (`q6asm-dai.c:193-197`) are never completed.
That is exactly what is measured: `periods` buffers, `peak=0`, then nothing. *(DSP-internal
behaviour: inference; the arithmetic and the frozen pointers are measured.)*

## 6. Fix

### 6.1 Minimal fix (runtime state — no rebuild): enable the codec's TX ports

`wcd->port_config[]` (and therefore `sdw_stream_add_slave()`'s port list) is filled only by these
controls, so they must be set **before** the PCM is opened:

```sh
amixer -c0 cset "ADC1 Switch" 1     # AMIC1 -> ADC1 -> SWR port 1 (SWR port number 2 per qcom,tx-port-mapping <2 3 4 5>)
amixer -c0 cset "ADC2 Switch" 1     # AMIC2 on the same SoundWire port, second channel (use 1 switch only for mono)
# alternatives for other inputs: DMIC0..3 Switch (port 3, shared with MBHC Switch), DMIC4..7 Switch (port 4)
```
The equivalent as a board route (what an ASoC UCM2 file for this card needs), diff-style:

```diff
--- /dev/null
+++ b/ucm2/conf.d/sm8250/Xiaomi-Redmi-K30-5G.conf   (or a local ~/.asoundrc hook)
+SectionDevice."Mic".0 {
+	Value {
+		EnableSequence.0 [
+			cset "name='ADC1 Switch' 1"
+			cset "name='ADC2 Switch' 1"
+		]
+	}
+}
```
Repeating the already-verified macro side is harmless (`MultiMedia2 Mixer TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3=1`,
`TX DEC0 MUX=SWR_MIC`, `TX SMIC MUX0=ADC0`, `TX_AIF1_CAP Mixer DEC0=1`, `TX_DEC0 Volume=84`).

### 6.2 Guard patch (recommended with 6.1): never stall silently again

```diff
--- a/sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x-sdw.c
+++ b/sound/soc/codecs/wcd938x-sdw.c
@@ int wcd938x_sdw_hw_params(struct wcd938x_sdw_priv *wcd,
 	wcd->sconfig.type = SDW_STREAM_PCM;
 
+	if (!wcd->active_ports) {
+		dev_err(&wcd->sdev->dev,
+			"no SoundWire data port enabled: set the codec's ADC*/DMIC*/MBHC Switch controls\n");
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
 	return sdw_stream_add_slave(wcd->sdev, &wcd->sconfig,
 				    &port_config[0], wcd->active_ports,
 				    wcd->sruntime);
```
With this, `arecord` fails at `hw_params` with a precise message instead of a timeout `EIO`.

### 6.3 Alternative / complement: stop swallowing ASM run failures

```diff
--- a/sound/soc/qcom/qdsp6/q6asm.c
+++ b/sound/soc/qcom/qdsp6/q6asm.c
@@ case APR_BASIC_RSP_RESULT:
 		case ASM_SESSION_CMD_RUN_V2:
+			if (result->status) {
+				dev_err(ac->dev, "ASM run failed: 0x%x\n", result->status);
+				ac->result = *result;
+				wake_up(&ac->cmd_wait);
+				goto done;
+			}
 			client_event = ASM_CLIENT_EVENT_CMD_RUN_DONE;
 			break;
```
This removes H3 from the equation for good (a rejected `RUN` currently looks exactly like a healthy
start).

### 6.4 Not a fix, but recorded: the DE-vote bug

`q6afe_vote_lpass_core_hw()` must capture the client handle from the VOTE response (store
`res->client_handle` in `q6afe_callback()`, then `*client_handle = afe->result.client_handle`) so
that `q6afe_unvote_lpass_core_hw()` stops sending 0. Cosmetic for capture (it only logs and leaks
the MACRO/DCODEC vote), but it is a real leak on every stream close.

## 7. Verification sequence (ends in `sox … stat`, RMS > 0.005)

Run from the host so that nothing is written on the phone (`sox` is not installed there); `-` is
stdout/stdin.

```sh
P=<lan-ip>; K=~/.ssh/picasso_key

# 1. prove the codec's TX ports are (before the fix: off -> values=off)
ssh -i $K root@$P 'amixer -c0 cget "ADC1 Switch"; amixer -c0 cget "ADC2 Switch"'

# 2. enable them (6.1) and keep the macro routing that already works
ssh -i $K root@$P 'amixer -c0 cset "ADC1 Switch" 1; amixer -c0 cset "ADC2 Switch" 1;
                   amixer -c0 cset "MultiMedia2 Mixer TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3" 1;
                   amixer -c0 cset "TX DEC0 MUX" SWR_MIC;
                   amixer -c0 cset "TX SMIC MUX0" ADC0;
                   amixer -c0 cset "TX_AIF1 CAP Mixer DEC0" 1;
                   amixer -c0 cset "TX_DEC0 Volume" 84'

# 3. fast discriminator: the stream must now survive more than 176 ms and more than 8 periods
ssh -i $K root@$P 'arecord -q -D hw:0,1 -f S16_LE -r 48000 -c 2 -d 3 /dev/null; echo RC=$?'
#    RC=0  -> data flows            RC=1 + "read error: Input/output error" -> still H1/H2/H4

# 4. signal proof, recorded on the host, measured with sox stat
ssh -i $K root@$P 'arecord -q -D hw:0,1 -f S16_LE -r 48000 -c 2 -d 5 -' \
  | sox -t wav - -n stat 2>&1 | grep -E "RMS +amplitude|Maximum amplitude"
#    pass: "RMS     amplitude: 0.0[0-9]+" with value > 0.005 (speak/tap near the mic; a quiet room
#    with 2.75 V mic bias at TX_DEC0 Volume 84 typically gives 0.01..0.1)

# 5. if step 3 still fails, H2/H4: enable the guard (6.2) and re-read
ssh -i $K root@$P 'dmesg | grep -iE "no SoundWire data port|AFE enable for port|routing for stream|ASM run failed"'
ssh -i $K root@$P 'cat /sys/bus/soundwire/devices/sdw:3:0:0217:010d:00:3/status'
```

Sanity checks to run alongside: `/proc/asound/card0/pcm1c/sub0/status` must show `hw_ptr` advancing
past `7679` and `tstamp` becoming non-zero; `grep lpass-tx-mclk /sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary`
must show `1 1` while recording.

## 8. What is *not* verified yet, and the one open risk

* **The codec switches' current value was not read back**: the phone dropped off the network
  (`ssh: connect to host <lan-ip> port 22: No route to host`, and all fallback addresses
  <lan-ip>/.112/.109/.88/.103, 10.77.71.2 went silent) right before this check, after ~40
  minutes of read-only probing and repeated `arecord` runs. No reset/flash/reboot was issued from
  this side. §7 step 1/2/3 is exactly the missing measurement; H1 predicts
  `values=off` → `RC=0` after enabling.
* If `arecord -d 3` still returns `EIO` after §7 step 2, then either H2 (AFE cdc-dma config) or H4
  (`sdw:3` stuck in `Alert`) holds; §6.2/§6.3 name the patches that make each distinguishable
  without guessing, and §4.5 gives the VA-DMIC path that sidesteps the SoundWire slave entirely.
